topics.topic: Whether alias disclosure and copy restrictions are determined by the field’s declared class or the alias’s actual identifying content
questions: When an alias contains a customer's name, contact data, address or another identifying characteristic, is its disclosure class determined permanently by the alias field or by the value it actually contains, and consequently do the no-agent, restriction and no-personal-data diagnostic guarantees still apply to that value?

Does R0-80 prohibit copies according to the actual value copied or only according to Registry's declared field class when a kept alias contains a name, address, tax id or other value R0-80 assigns exclusively to Registry?

When an alias actually contains a customer's name, address or other identifying value, does its field classification remain `business_confidential`, or do the value-based `personal_data` guarantees in R0-25, R0-26 and R0-80 forbid sending it to the agent and keeping it in another service?

Is an alias always `business_confidential` because of its field, even when its actual value is a person's name, address or other identifying characteristic, or does such content become `personal_data` and therefore have to be withheld from the agent and excluded from consumer snapshots?

quotes:
So an alias whose content breaks the rule does reach the agent and a
consumer's kept snapshot (R0-82), as a room name that breaks R0-68's rule
reaches the agent. This breaks neither R0-26 nor R0-80: the alias is held as
`business_confidential`, not `personal_data` (State 1, "Disclosure classes by
field"), and Registry's guarantees that no `personal_data` value reaches an
agent and that no other service keeps one cover the values it holds in that
class.
judgement.why: R0-90 expressly makes disclosure and copy restrictions depend on the alias field's declared class even when its content violates the writer rule.

topics.topic: How downstream snapshots and agent exposure must be remediated after a rule-breaking alias is corrected
questions: After the owner corrects a rule-breaking alias, what must happen to the old value already held in consumers' snapshots: must it be overwritten on the next read, actively invalidated or erased, or may it remain indefinitely?
After a violating alias is corrected or cleared in Registry, what must happen to the old value already held in a consumer snapshot or exposed to an agent session?

quotes:
Registry cannot tell a person's name from another word (R0-68), so
the one protection it gives the alias is its length; the owner's rule on its
content is the rest, and Registry promises nothing further about a value
that breaks it.
judgement.why: The text expressly promises no invalidation, erasure, replacement, or other remediation after a rule-breaking alias has reached an agent or consumer snapshot.

topics.topic: How an owner can replace or clear a rule-breaking alias in Registry
questions: What Registry action can the owner use to replace or clear an accepted alias after discovering that it contains a person's name, an address or another identifying value?

quotes:
'Correct a project' gives every editable fact of the project: display name,
   alias, customer link and the object — address, kind, characteristics
   (R0-45).

An optional fact the correction does not give is cleared; there is no
   partial correction.
judgement.why: State 2 specifies that the owner uses project correction to replace the alias and clears it by omitting that optional fact from the correction.
